extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers conducting reliability, validity, and measurement studies of clinical and public-health assessment tools
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria for designing, reporting, and evaluating reliability and validity of clinical and public-health measurement instruments (inter-rater, intra-rater, test–retest reliability; validity; measurement error; tool development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-based approach to abstracting unstructured EMR data
rubrics_metrics.description: A four step, phase-based approach including (1) team building, (2) identification of challenges, (3) adaptation of abstraction methods, and (4) systematic data quality monitoring, guided by a 'fit-for-use' framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to multi-site retrospective EMR abstraction of unstructured data (example: discharge communication for warfarin management). More time intensive than standard methods but markedly increased inter-rater reliability (kappas ≥ 0.89). Emphasises iterative adaptation and continuous data quality monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability assessment (SMOG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure reading grade level of patient-oriented materials using the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the reading grade level (example: SMOG=14.0). Compare to recommended/patient population literacy levels and interpret whether materials are too advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity assessment (PMOSE/iKIRSCH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify complexity and density of data (documents/layouts) using PMOSE/iKIRSCH scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report complexity score and corresponding interpretation (example: PMOSE/iKIRSCH=6.7 → 'low' complexity, requiring 8th–12th grade education). Use independent raters and report inter-rater agreement (e.g., Fleiss' kappa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability assessment (SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess suitability of health materials for intended audience using the Suitability Assessment of Materials (SAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report SAM percent score and categorical interpretation (example: 45% → 'adequate'). Use independent raters and report inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' kappa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability — Cohen's kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cohen's kappa (κ) to quantify inter-rater agreement for categorical items beyond chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report κ with 95% CI and interpret magnitude (examples in texts range from poor/fair/moderate/substantial/almost perfect). Also report item-specific kappas when instruments have multiple items. Note that prevalence and bias can affect κ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of agreement and observed positive/negative agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw percent agreement P(A) and observed percentage of positive agreement (Ppos) and negative agreement (Pneg) alongside κ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these metrics because they are intuitive and supplement κ (examples: P(A)=96%, Ppos=97%, Pneg=92%). Useful when prevalence is high or low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for continuous or ordinal scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC (report model and type, e.g., ICC(2,1) or ICC(2,3)) to quantify inter-rater, intra-rater, and test–retest reliability for continuous/scale measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC with 95% CI, specify model (two-way random, consistency/absolute agreement) and units (single measure vs average). Example thresholds cited: ICC ≥ 0.6 considered 'acceptable' in some reviews; many studies report ICCs ≥ 0.8 as excellent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test–retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess stability of instrument scores over time by re-administering and computing ICC (or other appropriate reliability metric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC for test–retest with confidence intervals; account for systematic differences between occasions. Example: ICC(2,1) for test–retest reported alongside inter-rater ICCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess consistency of a single rater's scores across repeated assessments (use ICC or κ as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report intra-rater ICC/κ and interpret alongside inter-rater values; video-based scoring may affect intra-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value
rubrics_metrics.description: For diagnostic or classification tasks, report sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV to describe accuracy relative to a reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide averages and standard deviations where multiple raters are involved (examples: sensitivity 53.0 ± 8.8%, specificity 61.2 ± 12.4%). Use when experts attempt classification (e.g., ultrasound pattern identification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency reliability (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cronbach's alpha to report internal consistency of multi-item scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alpha with interpretation (example: Cronbach's alpha = 0.94 interpreted as excellent). Combine with other evidence of unidimensionality (e.g., Rasch fit) rather than relying solely on alpha.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unidimensionality and construct validity (Rasch analysis, CFA, factor analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess scale structure and construct validity using Rasch analysis, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), or exploratory methods (PAF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report model fit statistics (e.g., Rasch chi-square and p-value), confirm whether hypothesized factor structure fits observed data, or report alternate factor solutions supported by data (examples: PAF supported two-factor AUDIT solution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal detectable change and measurement error (MDC, SE, LoA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report minimal detectable change (with confidence level, e.g., 90%) and other measurement error indices such as standard error (SE) and 95% limits of agreement (LoA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MDC to help interpret clinical relevance of score changes (example: MDC90 = 13 points). Report LoA widths (example: 5°–11°) and caution clinicians to consider measurement error when interpreting scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floor and ceiling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and report presence or absence of floor and ceiling effects in scale scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent at extremes; absence supports applicability across the measured spectrum (example: no floor or ceiling effects observed for DEMMI on admission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent validity (comparison with reference instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate validity by comparing new instrument scores with an established reference (concurrent validity), using ICCs, correlation, and LoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report concurrent ICCs and LoA; when appropriate, analyze coupling motions or multi-dimensional agreement metrics (examples: smartphone app vs electromagnetic tracking device ICCs 0.90–0.99).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement by category and tool-specific reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: When tools classify multiple categories (e.g., advertisement types, establishments), report percent agreement overall and by category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide category-level reliability (examples: overall reliability 69–89% across advertisement/establishment categories). Report number of items per category and range per site to inform context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard-setting method outcomes and reliability (norm-reference vs Angoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: When setting pass/fail standards for exams, compare methods (e.g., norm-reference 'mean −1 SD' versus modified Angoff) and report resulting pass rates and reliability of the standard-setting procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent agreement between methods and inter-rater/test–retest reliability for Angoff panels (examples: Angoff pass rate 100% vs norm-reference 85%; modified Angoff inter-rater reliability 0.81–0.82, test–retest 0.59–0.74).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of training and pilot rating phases to improve rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide rater training and consider a pilot rating/calibration phase after training to improve inter-rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report details of training and whether calibration/pilot phases were used. Studies indicate piloting following rater training may improve agreement (recommended for novice raters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study quality appraisal and evidence grading for reliability research
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess study risk of bias using standard checklists (e.g., Quality Appraisal of Reliability Studies) and synthesize overall evidence using approaches such as van Tulder's levels of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In systematic reviews, apply standardized bias checklists and grade overall evidence (examples: 'moderate' level of evidence for acceptable inter-rater ICCs). Report limitations such as poor reporting of rater blinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rater blinding and study reporting details
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report whether raters were blinded to each other's assessments and other methodological details that affect bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rater blinding (or lack thereof) and incomplete reporting can impact study quality and interpretation of reliability estimates; explicitly document these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample and rater heterogeneity for generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Design reliability studies with heterogeneous samples (e.g., multiple sites, varying ward types, heterogeneous participant demographics) and multiple raters to improve generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample characteristics (sites, participant types) and rater experience levels. Examples include multi-site designs across specialist and district hospitals to increase heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report prevalence and its influence on agreement statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report condition prevalence in the sample because prevalence affects agreement metrics (noted, e.g., prevalence=74% in MTSS study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prevalence alongside κ and P(A) to help interpret agreement measures and potential κ paradoxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-level reliability reporting for multi-domain observation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: For observation instruments with distinct domains (e.g., collaborative culture, environment, structure, risk management), report domain-level reliability (weighted κ) and total-score reliability (ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: weighted κ for collaborative culture=0.32 (low); environment items κ=0.78; total-score ICC=0.87. Lower agreement in some domains suggests need for clearer item definitions or rater training.
